sources.label: BFS STATPOP: permanent resident population by canton, 31 December 2025
BFS Structural Survey 2022, T 01.08.01.02: main languages by canton (residents aged 15+, multiple answers possible)

methodology: Estimated German-speaking residents = canton population (STATPOP 2025) x share of residents naming German or Swiss German as a main language (Structural Survey 2022). Dialect regions group cantons whose dialects are closest to the SwissDial recording; dialect borders do not follow canton borders, so region figures are approximations.

dialects.name: Zurich German
dialects.summary: The largest single dialect group and the variety most often heard in national media and business. Relatively close to other Midland dialects, which makes it a common default for Swiss German systems.
features: Initial k becomes ch: Chind = Kind, Chile = Kirche, cho = kommen
isch = ist, nöd = nicht, öppis = etwas, öpper = jemand, hüt = heute, mer = wir/man
Contractions: mitem = mit dem, uf de = auf der, d = die, e = ein/eine
Purpose clauses with zum ... z- + verb: zum go poschte = um einkaufen zu gehen
Passive with worde: isch gmacht worde = wurde gemacht

dialects.name: Bernese German
dialects.summary: Second-largest group and widely understood across Switzerland. Its l-vocalisation and nd-velarisation make it sound distinctive, but its vocabulary is close to Standard German.
features: l before consonants or at word end becomes u: Miuch = Milch, Wäut = Welt, vüu = viel, aui = alle
nd becomes ng: hinger = hinter, Ching = Kind, angers = anders, Hung = Hund
Unstressed endings often written with ä: machä = machen
I = ich, di = dich, nid = nicht, ir = in der, gäng = immer, öppe = etwa
Relative particle wo = der/die/das: dr Maa, wo dert steit = der Mann, der dort steht

dialects.name: Lucerne German
dialects.region_label: Central Switzerland (LU, ZG, SZ, UR, OW, NW)
dialects.summary: Represents the Central Swiss dialects around Lake Lucerne. Vowel lowering (u to o, i to e) is the most frequent source of recognition errors.
features: u becomes o and i becomes e in many words: ond = und, onder = unter, Hond = Hund, esch = ist, em = im
de = der/den, en = eine, ide = in der, ned = nicht
seit = sagt, sell = soll, werd = wird, gsi = gewesen
Enclitic pronouns: hesch = hast du, gömmer = gehen wir

dialects.name: Aargau German
dialects.summary: A transition zone between Bernese, Zurich and Basel dialects. The SwissDial speaker shows strong vowel lowering typical of the Freiamt and southern Aargau.
features: i becomes e and u becomes o (southern Aargau/Freiamt): emmer = immer, met = mit, esch = ist, om = um, ond = und
Enclitic pronouns: heter = hat er, hesch = hast du, chas = kann es
bem = beim, öpper = jemand, gha = gehabt, gsi = gewesen
Initial ch for k: Chind = Kind, Chopf = Kopf

dialects.name: St. Gallen German
dialects.summary: Represents the Eastern Swiss dialects. Faster speech rate and fused articles (dSchuel) are frequent sources of word-segmentation errors.
features: Fused articles: dSchuel = die Schule, dLüt = die Leute
nöd = nicht, de = der, uf = auf, abe = hinunter, ufe = hinauf, zwüsched = zwischen
luege = schauen, schaffe = arbeiten, go = gehen
z- + verb = zu + verb: zmache = zu machen; Johr = Jahr, erscht = erste

dialects.name: Basel German
dialects.summary: The only Low Alemannic dialect in SwissDial. Unlike most Swiss dialects it keeps initial k, so its sound differs markedly from Midland varieties. Basel-Landschaft speaks related Baselbieter dialects.
features: Initial k is kept (Kind, Kuchi = Küche) instead of ch
dr = der, d = die, e/ä = ein/eine, nit/nid = nicht, mr = mir/wir, me = man
hän = haben, goht = geht, stoht = steht, do = da/hier
Diminutive -li: Hüsli = Häuschen

dialects.name: Grisons German
dialects.summary: Chur Rhine Valley dialect with a clear, slow articulation. Characteristic a-endings and Romansh loanwords shape the transcript.
features: Unstressed -e/-en often become -a: macha = machen, schaffa = arbeiten, luaga = schauen
ua/ia diphthongs: guat = gut, muass = muss, dia = die, ma = man
hend = haben, kunnt = kommt, gsi = gewesen, nüt = nichts
Initial k often kept rather than ch

dialects.name: Valais German
dialects.summary: The most archaic and least mutually intelligible Swiss German dialect. It keeps full vowels in endings and old verb forms, so models frequently mistranscribe or mistranslate it despite its small speaker base.
features: Endings keep full vowels, often -u: läbu = leben, redu = reden
Plural verb forms often end in -unt or -nt
schich = sich, är = er, het = hat, nit = nicht, üs = aus, üf = auf
Diminutive -ji: Hüsji = Häuschen
Narrative perfect tense usually maps to the Standard German preterite
